memory_update.text: For renewables_storage_grid_integration, prioritize candidates by proximity to interconnection, BESS integration, inverter/control capability, grid equipment lead times, and dispatch/capacity monetization rather than renewable generation volume alone.
NEE, AES, FLNC, TSLA, ENPH, SEDG, GEV, ETN, HUBB, and PWR form the core above-$1B US-listed coverage map across developer/operator, storage, inverter, grid equipment, and grid construction layers.

Long-duration storage public coverage is weak: EOSE and STEM are included as small-cap/high-risk exceptions, but commercialization, financing, and customer-bankability evidence must be verified before treating them as chokepoint beneficiaries.

Private and non-US companies may dominate parts of the node, including battery cell supply, PCS/inverter hardware, EMS software, transformers, and HVDC equipment; US-listed proxies may be indirect or diversified.

node: Renewables, batteries, inverters, storage duration, and grid integration
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the renewables-storage-grid-integration node. The node is broader than renewable generation ownership: it includes utility-scale renewable developers with interconnection positions, battery energy storage system suppliers, inverter and power-electronics providers, grid equipment vendors, EPC/transmission contractors, software/control platforms, and selective long-duration storage challengers. This is research universe expansion only, not a buy/sell list. Stronger candidates tend to sit closer to interconnection, grid stability, storage attach rates, inverter capability, and monetization of volatility/capacity value.
